params.body:
## Why

On staging you can change something on the vehicle sheet, hit reload, and the typed values are
gone without a single question. There was supposed to be a guard; there were in fact two, and
neither covered the case Shane hit. While fixing it, two things that live in the same component
come along: "Volgende" walked past empty required fields (so you discovered on the last step that
the first one was never finished), and the action row / required-field legend needed straightening.

## What was wrong on each entry point

**Classic "add a vehicle"** (`ownstock/create.blade.php`, the flag-off path): no guard at all.
Nothing asked, ever. A reload after half an hour of typing was silently gone.

**Classic "edit a vehicle"** (`ownstock/edit.blade.php`): the guard existed, but it fired only if
a tab link had picked up the class `heeft-wijziging`. The marking is bound to `.nav-tabs.customtab`
and to five named panes, and it ignores anything that is not a *trusted* event - so an AI-filled
description, or a field in a pane outside that list, left the guard silent while there was real
unsaved work. The dot on the tab and the question at the door were one mechanism; they are two
different questions.

**Livewire sheet** (`App\Livewire\VehicleForm` + `livewire/vehicle-form.blade.php`): the
`beforeunload` handler had the right shape (`preventDefault` + `returnValue`) and `dirty` did become
true on a keystroke - but:
- a `bezigOpslaan` flag suppressed the guard from the moment you *pressed* Save, and nothing ever
  reset it when the save was **refused**. After a rejected save the sheet was full of unsaved work
  and the guard was switched off;
- `dirty` was never cleared after a save that **succeeded** (edit mode stays on the page), so a
  normal save-then-leave asked a pointless question;
- writes that do not come from a field event - the AI filling the descriptions, a button doing
  `$set` - did not mark the sheet dirty at all.

## What changed

**One guard for the classic forms.** New `<x-ui.unsaved-guard form="...">`, included by both
`ownstock/create.blade.php` and `ownstock/edit.blade.php`. It does not guess what "changed" means,
it *measures*: it records the field values and compares them on the way out. That is the only
definition that neither false-alarms (select2/iCheck/datepickers fire change events while the page
builds) nor misses a write the user did not type (the AI text). Two rules keep the measurement
honest: the recording is re-taken at the user's first real touch of the form (so late DOM writes by
the page itself never count), and fields that appeared or disappeared since are ignored (the sheet
adds and removes rows). The tab-dot marking stays in `edit.blade.php` as its own, separate thing.
`window.slSkipUnloadGuard` stays the escape hatch for navigation the app itself does after saving.

**The Livewire sheet.** `bezigOpslaan` is gone - a flag that turns the guard off on the way *into*
a save and never comes back is worse than no guard. Instead: `dirty` clears only when the server
says something was saved (`vehicle-saved`, dispatched by `save()` on success and by `saveStep()`
after the draft write), and it is set by any real edit *plus* any Livewire commit that carries
property updates - which is exactly what an AI fill or a `$set` is.

**"Volgende" now judges the step you are leaving.** `saveStep()` does two things in a fixed order,
and the order is the point: (1) it always writes the sheet to the draft row, also when the step is
about to be refused - PR 287's lesson, a refusal must never cost what was typed; (2) then it
validates, using only the rules of the fields on *that* step (`fieldsForStep()`), never the whole
sheet. `required` now counts. A refusal keeps you on the step, names the missing fields the way the
sheet already does (`fieldLabels()`, the block at the top plus the per-field message), and puts the
cursor on the first one. Going back is untouched and free; "Opslaan" keeps its meaning.
Amounts use the same normalisation as the save door (`prepareForValidation` ->
`OwnStockService::normaliseAmounts`), so an untouched `export_price` ("Eindklant") does not block a
step. **Editing an existing vehicle keeps navigating freely** - `saveStep()` returns early in edit
mode as it always did. That is deliberate: the sections of a published vehicle are navigation, not
a wizard, and turning them into gates would stop a dealer from reaching the photo tab of a car whose
data someone else left incomplete.

**Action row.** One right-aligned row, always in the same order: saved-at note, Vorige, Volgende,
primary action rightmost. On the first step Vorige is invisible but keeps its place, so nothing
shifts when it appears on step 2. On a narrow phone the existing two-column grid is kept, including
"no Vorige on step one, so Volgende takes the full width".

**Legend.** `* = verplicht veld` moves from a red 11px `<small>` glued to the field above into the
muted helper register (`ui-field-help`, 12px, brand-faint) with room above, via a shared
`<x-ui.required-legend>` - it was written out three times in three tab partials.

## What is tested versus checked by hand

**Tested** (`tests/Feature/UnsavedChangesGuardTest.php`, `tests/Feature/VehicleFormStepTest.php`):
- the guard component renders `preventDefault()` **and** `returnValue = ''` (a browser needs both),
  hooks `form.submit` (the real save path does not fire the submit event), and stands down while
  submitting;
- both classic entry points include the guard;
- the Livewire sheet renders its `beforeunload` handler on every step (general, prices, dates, extras);
- a successful save dispatches `vehicle-saved` (the flag clears); a **refused** save does not;
- "Volgende" refuses a step with an empty required field of that step and names the field;
- the typed values survive that refusal, on the component **and** in the draft row;
- "Volgende" moves on once the step is filled; an untouched amount does not block; a required field
  of *another* step does not block this one; going back is never refused; editing navigates freely.

All five of the load-bearing behaviours were mutation-checked (write-after-validate, stripping
`required` again, dropping the amount normalisation, removing `preventDefault`, not dispatching
`vehicle-saved`); each mutation fails exactly the test that covers it.

**Checked by hand in a real browser** (Playwright against `artisan serve`, Chrome, fixture dealer +
vehicle, both with the Livewire flag on and off) - a browser-level assertion of the native dialog is
not something CI can hold:
- classic add: a clean page does not ask, an edited page does, and Chrome really shows its own
  "Leave site?" dialog on reload (navigation blocked until the dialog was answered);
- classic edit: same, and reverting a field back to its original value makes the question go away;
- Livewire sheet: typing asks; a `$set` from outside a field asks; a successful save makes it stop
  asking;
- create flow: "Volgende" on an empty first step stays on the step, shows
  "Nog 1 verplicht veld niet ingevuld: Chassisnummer (VIN)" and focuses that field; filling it moves
  on and the guard stands down;
- action row and legend at 1280 and 390 (order stable, Volgende does not shift between step 1 and 2,
  mobile grid unchanged).

## Notes for the reviewer

- `tests/Feature/VehicleFormSaveTest.php` carried two assertions that encoded the *old* contract
  ("next saves the step without demanding the required fields", and a walk-through that advanced
  past an empty 'general'). Both were rewritten to the new intent rather than deleted: the draft
  write is still asserted, the refusal is now asserted next to it. One test that main added this
  morning (`next on a step without rules ...`) leaned on standing on 'type' with an empty chassis;
  it now fills the chassis first, with a line saying why.
- Unrelated and not touched: the sheet logs `uiAutogrow is not defined` when a step containing a
  textarea arrives through a Livewire morph (the component's `@once` script never reached the
  first page render). Worth a separate look.
- Branched and rebased on `main` at 6a15523.
params.title: Vehicle sheet: ask before leaving unsaved work
